title: The Twenty-Seventh of October
subtitle: Roosevelt's Birthday
intro: He was born on 27 October 1858 and married on the same date twenty-two years later. He spent one birthday walking the grounds with a bullet in his chest, against his wife's explicit wishes. Ten questions for the day itself.

questions.prompt: On what date was Theodore Roosevelt born?
questions.explanation: 27 October 1858, in New York City — the second of four children and the first son of Theodore Roosevelt Sr. and Martha Bulloch Roosevelt. January 6 is the date he died, sixty years later.
questions.imageAlt: Theodore Roosevelt as a small boy
questions.credit: Theodore Roosevelt, about two years old. Theodore Roosevelt Collection, Houghton Library, Harvard University.

options: A brownstone at 28 East 20th Street, Manhattan
questions.explanation: A five-storey brownstone on East 20th Street, in a fashionable stretch of Manhattan. The house was pulled down in 1916 and rebuilt as a memorial after his death; it stands today as the Theodore Roosevelt Birthplace National Historic Site.
questions.imageAlt: Theodore Roosevelt's birthplace at 28 East 20th Street, New York
questions.credit: Theodore Roosevelt's birthplace, 28 East 20th Street, New York. Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division.

options: He was elected to the Assembly
questions.explanation: He married Alice Hathaway Lee in the Unitarian church at Brookline, Massachusetts, on his twenty-second birthday. He had pursued her relentlessly for two years, and he chose the date.
questions.imageAlt: Alice Hathaway Lee, the first Mrs. Theodore Roosevelt
questions.credit: The first Mrs. Theodore Roosevelt (Alice Hathaway Lee). Theodore Roosevelt Collection, Houghton Library, Harvard University.

questions.prompt: As a boy, what delighted him about one particular birthday morning?
options: It snowed for the first time on his birthday
He was given his first rifle
His father returned from a long absence
questions.explanation: A snowstorm on the night of 26 October. His family recorded that Teedie was delighted to have had snow on his birthday morning, never having had that before. He was a boy who kept records of things, and this went in the record.
questions.imageAlt: Tintype of the four Roosevelt children
questions.credit: The Roosevelt children. Theodore Roosevelt Collection, Houghton Library, Harvard University.

questions.prompt: In 1912 his birthday fell thirteen days after a significant event. What?
options: He had been shot in the chest in Milwaukee
He had lost the presidential election
He had founded the Progressive Party
questions.explanation: A saloonkeeper shot him at close range in Milwaukee on 14 October; he delivered his speech before going to hospital. Edith made him stay indoors for three days. On his birthday he went out to walk the grounds anyway, to her considerable displeasure. He called the resting mollycoddling.
questions.imageAlt: Roosevelt with Rough Rider veterans during the Bull Moose campaign
questions.credit: T.R. with Rough Rider veterans during the Bull Moose campaign, Chicago. Theodore Roosevelt Collection, Houghton Library, Harvard University.

questions.prompt: What did Henry Cabot Lodge write to him on his forty-sixth birthday in 1904?
options: "You have made a very good start in life"
questions.explanation: "You have made a very good start in life and your friends have great hopes for you when you grow up." Lodge was his closest political friend for thirty years, and the joke lands because Roosevelt was, at forty-six, already a former governor, a war hero and the sitting president.
questions.imageAlt: Theodore Roosevelt in his private office
questions.credit: Theodore Roosevelt, 26th President of the United States, in his private office. Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division.

questions.prompt: That 1904 birthday came shortly before what?
options: The election that made him president in his own right
The founding of the Forest Service
questions.explanation: The November 1904 election, which he won handsomely — the first time he had been elected president rather than inheriting the office. On election night he announced he would not accept another nomination, a promise he kept in 1908 and regretted almost immediately.
questions.imageAlt: Campaign poster for Theodore Roosevelt and Charles W. Fairbanks
questions.credit: For President, Theodore Roosevelt; For Vice President, Charles W. Fairbanks. Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division.

questions.prompt: How old was he when he became president?
questions.explanation: Forty-two, and still the youngest person ever to hold the office. He reached it by succession after McKinley's assassination — the youngest man ever elected to the presidency was John F. Kennedy, at forty-three.
questions.imageAlt: Vice President Roosevelt at the swearing in of President McKinley, March 1901
questions.credit: Vice-President Roosevelt at the swearing in of President McKinley, March 1901. Theodore Roosevelt Collection, Houghton Library, Harvard University.

questions.prompt: What did his family call him as a boy?
questions.explanation: Teedie. His father was Thee and his eldest son would be Ted. He disliked Teddy all his life — that one belonged to the newspapers, not the family.
questions.imageAlt: Theodore Roosevelt at about two years old
questions.credit: Theodore Roosevelt, about two years old. Theodore Roosevelt Collection, Houghton Library, Harvard University.

questions.prompt: How many birthdays did he have in all?
questions.explanation: Sixty. He died in his sleep at Sagamore Hill on 6 January 1919, ten weeks after his sixtieth birthday. Vice President Marshall remarked that death had to take him sleeping, because awake there would have been a fight.
questions.credit: The Parlor, Sagamore Hill. Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division.
